consensus_summary: Consensus primary identification is the Church (or believer) as the lesser light that has no light of its own but reflects Christ’s light (the sun); secondary common uses are apocalyptic portents (darkened/blood moon), Mary, Israel/family, seasons, and permanence.
book_summary: Moon is the faithful witness—the reflecting, submissive side of a relationship—picturing the Son submitting to and reflecting the Father, the wife submitting to her husband, and the Church submitting to Christ.
consensus_core_identification: Church/believer as reflector of Christ’s light
book_core_identification: Faithful witness / reflecting-submissive partner in hierarchical relationships
boundary_disagreement: Consensus largely restricts the reflector motif to Church (or Mary/Israel); book keeps that case but extends the same reflecting-submissive pattern to Son–Father and wife–husband and centers the definition on ‘faithful witness’ rather than light alone.
material_contradiction: None; the book explicitly notes and retains the common Church-reflecting-Christ reading as one instance of its broader pattern.
rationale: Both share the core notion of derived/reflected light and submission. The book does not replace the consensus referent; it generalizes it into a relational archetype (faithful witness) whose extension properly includes additional pairs (Son/Father, wife/husband) while still covering the Church case. This is boundary/precision change, not core contradiction or pure novelty.
strongest_objection: Psalm 89:37’s ‘faithful witness’ traditionally signals covenantal permanence, not a multi-level submission typology, and applying ‘moon’ to the Son (normally the sun) stretches the usual Christological assignment.
